findings.fix: Raise the stock-db Deployment's memory request/limit well above 24Mi (e.g. 256Mi or more) so it survives loading the stock index and stays up for stock-api.

diagnosis.summary: stock-api crash-loops with 'stock-db:5432 unreachable' because its database, stock-db, is itself crash-looping: the container is repeatedly OOMKilled (exit 137) on a 24Mi memory limit while loading the stock index into memory. Root cause is the undersized memory limit in the stock-db Deployment; stock-api is the victim. Fix: raise stock-db's memory limit.

findings.name: orders-api

diagnosis.summary: orders/orders-api is crash-looping (5 restarts, exit code 1, BackOff events). Container log shows 'FATAL: DATABASE_URL is not set'; the pod spec has no env or envFrom at all, so the missing database URL is a config gap in the orders-api Deployment. findings.name: mailer
findings.root_cause: mailer crash-loops with 'nc: bad address smtp-relay' because its pod template sets dnsPolicy: None and points at a nonexistent nameserver 10.96.0.99, so the Service name smtp-relay never resolves — even though the relay itself is up.
findings.fix: In the mailer Deployment pod template, remove the custom dnsConfig and set dnsPolicy back to ClusterFirst (or point nameservers at the real cluster DNS service IP) so smtp-relay.svc.cluster.local resolves.

diagnosis.summary: The smtp-relay is NOT down: its pod is Running/Ready, listening on port 25, and the Service has 1 ready endpoint (25->25). The failure is on the mailer side: its pod template overrides DNS with dnsPolicy: None and a bogus nameserver 10.96.0.99, so lookups of 'smtp-relay' fail ('nc: bad address'), the relay check loop gives up, and the container exits 1 and restarts. Fix the mailer Deployment's DNS config (restore ClusterFirst or use the real cluster DNS IP).

diagnosis.summary: The nightly-export Job in exports failed both attempts: each pod exited with code 2 after logging 'ERROR: permission denied: cannot write /exports/orders-2026-09-27.csv'. The Job reached BackoffLimitExceeded, so no export file was produced. Root cause is the export container lacking write permission to its output path; fix by giving it a writable destination (permissions or a mounted volume) and re-running the job.

findings.name: defaults
findings.root_cause: statement-builder's Deployment declares no memory resources, so the namespace LimitRange 'defaults' injects a 32Mi memory limit (and 16Mi request); the workload's build step buffers ~50MB in memory, exceeds the injected 32Mi limit, and the kernel OOM-kills the container (exit 137) in a restart loop.
findings.fix: Raise the default memory limit in LimitRange finance/defaults (e.g. to >=128Mi), or set an explicit memory limit on the statement-builder Deployment container large enough for its ~50MB working set.

diagnosis.summary: statement-builder in finance is crash-looping with OOMKilled (exit 137, 3 restarts) even though its Deployment sets no memory limit. The namespace LimitRange 'defaults' injects a 32Mi memory limit / 16Mi request into containers that declare none, and the workload's build step holds ~50MB in memory, exceeding that injected limit. Root cause object to change: LimitRange finance/defaults (or set an explicit adequate limit on the Deployment).

findings.name: ledger
findings.root_cause: ledger container exits 2 on startup with 'panic: invalid config key "retries": expected integer, got "three"' — the app's configuration (embedded in its command) holds a non-integer value for retries, so it crash-loops and never becomes ready.
findings.fix: Correct the ledger configuration so the 'retries' key is an integer (e.g. 3) instead of the string 'three', then roll the Deployment.

findings.name: ledger-api
findings.root_cause: Service ledger-api selects app=ledger-gateway but no pod carries that label (the healthy backend pods are labeled app=ledger-api), so it has 0 matching pods and 0 ready endpoints and cannot answer.
findings.fix: Change the Service selector to app=ledger-api (or relabel the ledger-api Deployment pods to app=ledger-gateway) so it selects the running nginx pods.

diagnosis.summary: Two independent faults in namespace ledger. (1) The ledger Deployment crash-loops: its container exits 2 immediately with 'panic: invalid config key \"retries\": expected integer, got \"three\"' — an app config error, not a resource or image problem. (2) Service ledger-api does not answer because its selector app=ledger-gateway matches zero pods; the actual backend Deployment ledger-api (nginx, 1/1 ready) labels its pods app=ledger-api, so the service has no endpoints."

findings.name: checkout
findings.root_cause: Service 'checkout' uses selector app=checkout-v2, but the running pods are labeled app=checkout, so the selector matches no pods and the service has zero endpoints — clients get connection refused even though the pod itself is healthy.
findings.fix: Update the Service selector to app=checkout (or relabel the Deployment's pod template with app=checkout-v2) so it matches the running pods.

diagnosis.summary: Checkout pods are Running/Ready, but Service 'checkout' selects app=checkout-v2 while pods carry app=checkout, leaving the service with 0 ready endpoints → connection refused for callers. Fix by aligning the Service selector with the pod labels.

findings.name: report-worker
findings.root_cause: Container is OOMKilled (exit 137) seconds after start because its memory limit is only 32Mi; the workload's own 'warming report cache' step plus tail /dev/zero exceed that limit, so no app error ever appears in logs — the kernel kills it before it can print anything.
findings.fix: Raise the report-worker container memory limit (and request) above actual warm-cache usage, e.g. limit 256Mi / request 128Mi, or reduce what the cache-warming step allocates.

diagnosis.summary: reports/report-worker restarts every few seconds with no log output: the container is OOMKilled (exit code 137) within ~15s of starting because its 32Mi memory limit is too small for its work ('warming report cache'; tail /dev/zero). Pod state and BackOff events confirm repeated OOMKills; deployment shows 0 ready replicas. Fix is to raise the memory limit/request on the Deployment.

findings.name: cache
findings.root_cause: Pod cache-54f4fcc74-25gpc stays Pending/Unschedulable because its nodeSelector requires disktype=nvme, while the only node doctor-lab-control-plane is labeled disktype=standard, so no node matches.
findings.fix: Remove or correct the nodeSelector on the cache Deployment (change disktype=nvme to disktype=standard, or drop it); alternatively label/provision an nvme node.

diagnosis.summary: The cache deployment never schedules a pod: its pod template carries nodeSelector disktype=nvme, but the sole cluster node doctor-lab-control-plane has disktype=standard. The scheduler reports '1 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector' and the pod remains Pending with 0/1 ready replicas. Fix is in the Deployment spec (nodeSelector), not the node.

findings.name: ml-trainer
findings.root_cause: ml-trainer pod requests 64 CPUs but the cluster's only node has 2 allocatable CPUs, so the scheduler reports '1 Insufficient cpu' and the pod stays Pending; preemption is not helpful.
findings.fix: Lower the ml-trainer CPU request to fit the cluster (e.g. 500m–1cpu on this 2-CPU node), or add a larger node before scaling up.

diagnosis.summary: ml-trainer has been Pending because its pod requests 64 CPUs while the single cluster node (doctor-lab-control-plane) offers only 2 allocatable CPUs. Scheduler events confirm 'Insufficient cpu' with no taints or constraints involved. Fix: reduce the Deployment's CPU request to fit available capacity or provision more nodes.

findings.name: pricing-api
findings.root_cause: Client calls to the pricing-api Service fail with connection refused because the Service targets port 8080, but the pricing-api container only listens on containerPort 80; traffic forwarded to 8080 hits a closed port even though the pod is healthy and ready.
findings.fix: Set the Service targetPort to 80 (matching the container's containerPort) or change the app to listen on 8080.

diagnosis.summary: pricing-api pods are healthy and ready, but the Service pricing-api maps port 80 -> targetPort 8080 while the nginx container only listens on containerPort 80. Forwarded connections hit a closed port, so clients (e.g. the traffic probe) get 'Connection refused' against the ClusterIP 10.96.163.4. Root cause: wrong targetPort in the Service spec.

findings.name: web
findings.root_cause: The web Deployment's readiness probe does HTTP GET / on port 8081, but the nginx container listens on its default port 80 (no containerPort/config override); every probe gets connection refused, so the pod stays NotReady and the deployment is 0/1 with no traffic.
findings.fix: Point the readiness probe at the port nginx actually serves (port 80), or configure nginx to listen on 8081; then the pod becomes Ready and receives traffic.

diagnosis.summary: web/web-7969d6cc4c-46fdj runs nginx fine (started, workers up) but its readiness probe hits http://:8081/, while nginx serves on port 80 — probes fail with connection refused (25 warnings), so the pod is NotReady and the Deployment shows 0/1 ready, receiving no traffic. Fix: align the probe port with the container's actual listening port (or vice versa).

findings.name: team-quota
findings.root_cause: Scaling renderer to 5 pods is blocked because the namespace ResourceQuota team-quota caps pods at 2 (used: 2), so every new pod creation by ReplicaSet renderer-85d9d4b59d is rejected with 'exceeded quota' and only 2 of 5 replicas run.
findings.fix: Raise the pods limit in ResourceQuota batch/team-quota from 2 to at least 5 (or move renderer to a namespace/quota that allows it), then re-check the rollout.

diagnosis.summary: renderer Deployment in batch wants 5 replicas but only 2 exist. The deployment's ReplicaFailure condition and repeated FailedCreate events show pod creation is forbidden: exceeded quota team-quota, requested pods=1, used=2, limited=2. The ResourceQuota confirms hard pods=2, used=2. Fix is to raise the quota's pods limit; no pod or image problem exists.

findings.name: reporting-api
findings.root_cause: reporting-api requests 300m CPU / 256Mi but observed usage is ~0m CPU and 3Mi memory across all samples, leaving ~$7.69/month of idle request cost
findings.fix: lower reporting-api container requests to 10m CPU / 8Mi (≈1.5–2× the 0m/3Mi p95); re-check after a longer sample window since usage was near-zero for the whole 2-minute window

diagnosis.summary: Rightsize audit of analytics: reporting-api is over-provisioned (requests 300m/256Mi vs ~0m/3Mi used; ~$7.69/mo idle) — recommend 10m/8Mi, medium confidence because the sample window is short and usage was near-zero throughout. Not flagged: cache (only ~$0.25/mo idle, not material) and ingest-worker (pinned at its 50m CPU limit in every sample — throttled, never cut). No problem pods in the namespace.

findings.name: catalog
findings.root_cause: Hotfix rollout stuck: new ReplicaSet pod catalog-58664cc6f-bhmp9 is in ImagePullBackOff because image "nginx:1.29-alpine-hotfix" does not exist in docker.io/library (ErrImagePull, NotFound), so the old nginx:1.29-alpine@sha256:5616... pods keep serving and users still see the old version.
findings.fix: Point the Deployment at a valid hotfix image (correct registry/repository/tag that actually exists, e.g. your internal registry path or the real tag) and re-rollout; if the image must come from docker.io, verify the tag name first.

diagnosis.summary: Catalog hotfix deploy is stuck: the new pod can't pull image nginx:1.29-alpine-hotfix (NotFound in docker.io/library), so the rolling update never completes (ProgressDeadlineExceeded) and the two old-version replicas remain available — which is why users still see the old version. Fix the image reference in the catalog Deployment to an existing image.

findings.name: search-web
findings.root_cause: The liveness probe runs a busy-loop (300k shell iterations) before the wget check with timeoutSeconds=1, so it always times out; kubelet kills the healthy container every few minutes, producing CrashLoopBackOff with exit code 0 and no app errors in logs.
findings.fix: Remove the busy-loop from the liveness exec command (or replace the probe with an httpGet on port 80) so the probe completes within its 1s timeout.

diagnosis.summary: search-web restarts because its liveness probe is broken, not the app. The exec probe runs `sh -c i=0; while [ $i -lt 300000 ]; do i=$((i+1)); done; wget ...` with timeoutSeconds=1; events show "Liveness probe failed: command timed out" repeatedly, and kubelet kills the container ("failed liveness probe, will be restarted"), which exits with code 0 — hence no errors in logs and CrashLoopBackOff. Fix is to correct the probe in the search-web Deployment.

findings.name: auth-api-cert
findings.root_cause: session-svc proxies /login to https://auth-api:443 and rejects the handshake because auth-api's serving certificate (issued by Internal Services CA 2026) expired on 2026-09-26, so every login returns 502 with 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)'
findings.fix: Re-issue the auth-api serving certificate from Internal Services CA 2026 (it expired 2026-09-26), update the auth-api-tls secret, and restart the auth-api pods

diagnosis.summary: Logins fail with 502 through session-svc because upstream auth-api serves an expired TLS cert. session-svc logs show 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (10:certificate has expired)' for GET /login to https://auth-api:443 → 502. Cert in ConfigMap auth-api-cert (CN=auth-api, issuer Internal Services CA 2026) expired 2026-09-26; the CA itself is valid ~10 years, so this is leaf expiry, not a trust mismatch. Pods run and are ready — only the cert needs renewal."

diagnosis.summary: payments-api is up (pod Running/Ready). The 502s come from checkout-web: nginx logs show 'upstream SSL certificate verify error: (21:unable to verify the first certificate)' when proxying /pay. checkout-web mounts legacy-ca ('Legacy Services CA 2021') as its trust store, but the post-migration API cert is signed by 'Internal Services CA 2026' (internal-ca ConfigMap). Fix: make checkout-web trust Internal Services CA 2026.
